column1: # Chinese wording of 성어 whose CC-CEDICT headword differs from the Korean hanja (after character variants): Korean hanja -> CEDICT traditional headword.
# Only rows whose review column says `approved...` ship (data/seongeo_zh_alias.tsv is read by src/seongeo_zh.rs); see qa/seongeo_zh_alias_review.md.

# Columns: hanja (as in seongeo_en_equiv.tsv) | cedict (traditional headword of the SAME idiom in CC-CEDICT) | note (why it is the same idiom, confidence) | review (draft | approved... | rejected: reason).
# Rule: the Chinese chengyu must be the same idiom (same story / image / meaning), not merely a similar one. A row whose headword is not in CEDICT simply matches nothing.

column3: note
Same fable (the old man who lost his horse); Korean writes 之, Chinese 失. High confidence.
Same image (splitting bamboo); word order differs. High confidence.
Same idiom (a rabble like crows gathered); Korean 卒 (soldier) vs Chinese 眾 (crowd). High confidence.
Same story (Liu Bei visits Zhuge Liang three times); 草廬 vs 茅廬 are the same thatched hut. High confidence.
Same image (bamboo shoots / spring shoots after rain); 竹 vs 春. High confidence.
Same saying (good things are beset by obstacles); 魔 is the Korean spelling of 磨. High confidence.
Same idiom (the sea becomes mulberry fields); order and 碧/滄 differ. High confidence.

Same idiom (share joys and hardships). High confidence. Reviewer (2026-11-24): hold. 同甘共苦 is the Chinese equivalent, not the same idiom: different wording and image (sweet/bitter vs bitter/joy), no shared source text; Korean has its own 동감공고(同甘共苦).

Same idiom (ungrateful, forgetting a benefactor). High confidence. Reviewer (2026-11-24): hold. 忘恩負義 is an equivalent with different wording (負義 vs 忘德) and no shared source; Korean has its own 망은부의(忘恩負義). Same meaning, not the same idiom.
Same idiom (indecisive); 不 vs 寡. High confidence.
Same idiom (return home in glory); word order differs. High confidence.

Same pair of repayment stories (knotted grass; ring in the beak); Korean keeps only the first, so the equivalence is by tradition. Medium confidence. Reviewer (2026-11-24): hold. 結草銜環 joins two stories (結草 from 左傳 + 銜環 of 楊寶); Korean 結草報恩 has only the first. Overlapping, not the same idiom.
Same idiom (treat with new respect after a transformation); 對 vs 看. Medium-high confidence.
Same idiom (fight on alone); 鬪 vs 戰. Medium-high confidence (CEDICT may also list 孤軍奮鬥, which the variant step finds first).
Same idiom (myriad forms); 象 vs 狀. Medium-high confidence.
Same idiom (looks down on everyone); 眼下 vs 目中. Medium confidence.
Same phrase (a splendid land); 江 vs 河. Medium confidence.

Same saying (autumn: the sky is high, horses are fat); 天 vs 秋. Medium confidence. Reviewer: same source line (杜審言 秋高塞馬肥); CEDICT also notes the old "season for military campaigns" nuance, but the image and the core meaning (fine autumn weather) match.
Same idiom (adapt to circumstances); 臨 vs 隨 (CEDICT may list 臨機應變 itself, which then matches exactly first). Medium-high confidence.
